blocks.text: The long register is more than a modern-style census. Its family groups, priestly eligibility questions, temple-related workers, singers, animals, and gifts present the returned community as an ordered whole with continuity from those who first returned. At the same time, the relationship of this list to the parallel list in Ezra 2, along with uncertainty about ancient counting, means its totals should not be treated as a precise modern census without qualification.

The first-person account in the preceding chapters gives way here to a documentary register. This fits a wider pattern in Nehemiah: the book contains vivid first-person material alongside third-person narration, lists, material also found in Ezra, and editorial transitions. It is therefore too simple to read the whole book either as a single uninterrupted autobiography or as wholly fictionalized narrative.
